Why go: the classic sights, plus a paddle through the mangroves

Most Samui safaris end at a viewpoint or temple. This one ends on the water. After the Big Buddha, Wat Plai Laem, lunch with a view, the Hin Ta and Hin Yai rocks, a swim at Na Muang waterfall and a short rubber-tapping demonstration, the group swaps the jeep for kayaks and paddles through a mangrove channel with a guide. It is a quiet end to a busy day, and a side of the island most visitors never see.

The jeep takes no more than 12 guests, and entrance fees are included, so there is nothing to pay on the day except drinks.

Who it suits, and who should choose something else

  • Good for: families with children from 5, couples, and anyone who wants the main sights and some activity in one day.
  • Choose something else if you have toddlers (minimum age 5) or prefer a shorter day; the jungle discovery safari ends at 16:00.
  • Want more time on the water? See our kayak and SUP guide.

Good to know

  • Mangroves: keep hands inside the kayak near the roots and don't touch crabs or mudskippers. Mosquitoes are active late in the afternoon.
  • Waterfall safety: Na Muang's rocks are slippery; swim only where the guide shows you.
  • Temples: cover shoulders and knees at the Big Buddha and Wat Plai Laem.
  • Weather: showers are frequent from October to December, but the route is mostly sheltered.

How the day is paced

The morning is about temples and is mostly short walks from the jeep. The afternoon is more active: a swim at the waterfall, then the paddle. Pack swimwear under your clothes from the start, keep a dry T-shirt in a bag for the drive home, and eat a proper lunch, as the kayak comes late in the day when energy dips.
